question:
A 5-day-old neonate is brought to the pediatrician by his parents for yellow skin for the past few days. His parents also reported that he remains quiet all day and does not even respond to sound. Further perinatal history reveals that he was born by cesarean section at 36 weeks of gestation, and his birth weight was 2.8 kg (6.1 lb). This baby is the second child of this couple, who are close relatives. Their first child died as the result of an infection at an early age. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 116/min, and respirations are 29/min. On physical examination, hypotonia is present. His laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.9 gm/dL
Leukocyte count 9,300/mm3
Platelet count 170,000/mm3
Unconjugated bilirubin 33 mg/dL
Conjugated bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL
Coombs test Negative
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Neonate with yellow skin and hypotonia" -> "Possible neonatal jaundice" -> "High unconjugated bilirubin levels" -> "Phototherapy indicated" -> 95% CHAIN: "Neonate with yellow skin and hypotonia" -> "High unconjugated bilirubin levels" -> "Possible hemolytic disease of the newborn" -> "Phototherapy indicated" -> 90% CHAIN: "Neonate with yellow skin and hypotonia" -> "High unconjugated bilirubin levels" -> "Negative Coombs test" -> "Phototherapy indicated" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The neonate presents with yellow skin, hypotonia, and high unconjugated bilirubin levels. Given the negative Coombs test, phototherapy is indicated for the management of neonatal jaundice in this case.
analysis: The neonate is presenting with jaundice, hypotonia, and high unconjugated bilirubin levels, indicating a likely case of neonatal jaundice. Given the negative Coombs test, which rules out hemolytic disease of the newborn, the most appropriate next step is to initiate phototherapy to manage the hyperbilirubinemia.
